tasks.title: index: the twelve-language table, proven against the loaded grammars

details.goal: The language layer as DATA, ported row for row, with the probe test that proves every declared node type exists in the grammar the binary will actually load — the Rust replacement for tests/lang.test.ts.
details.contract:
Port `src/indexer/lang/{types,registry}.ts` (250 lines) row for row. Types:
```rust
pub enum LangId { Python, TypeScript, Tsx, JavaScript, Go, Java, Rust, C, Cpp, CSharp, Php, Ruby }
pub struct LangRow { pub id: LangId, pub extensions: &'static [&'static str],
  pub class_types: &'static [&'static str], pub function_types: &'static [&'static str],
  pub import_types: &'static [&'static str], pub call_types: &'static [&'static str],
  pub inheritance_types: &'static [&'static str], pub test_file_regex: Option<&'static str> }
pub fn detect_language(path: &str) -> Option<LangId>;   // extension only, lowercased, first row wins
pub fn spec_for(id: LangId) -> &'static LangRow;
pub fn tree_sitter_language(id: LangId) -> tree_sitter::Language;
```
The 12 rows (extensions, and the five node-type lists) are copied VERBATIM from the registry, including the empty `inheritanceTypes` for C and the `testFileRegex` per row; the `grammarWasm` field becomes `tree_sitter_language`, which returns the crate's `LANGUAGE` constant per id.
`tests/lang.rs` is the port of `tests/lang.test.ts`: for EVERY declared node type of all 12 rows, parse a small snippet that should contain it and assert (a) the grammar's `node_kinds` contains the name and (b) the parsed tree actually contains a node of that kind. A missing name is a test failure, never a comment. Where a native grammar genuinely lacks a name the WASM bundle had, record the substitution in `registry.rs` with a comment stating the measured effect, list it in `AGENTS.md`'s gaps file, and say so in the task report — do not silently drop the type.
Also port `detectLanguage`'s quirks: lowercasing, `""` -> None, `.d.ts` resolving to typescript, and first-row-wins for a shared extension.
steps: Port types.rs and the extension map/registry with all 12 rows.
Map each LangId to its grammar crate's `LANGUAGE`.
Write the snippet per language that exercises each declared node type.
Write the probe test; make it fail loudly with the language and the missing name.
Record any substitution and the measured consequence.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-index --test lang` exits 0 and prints the number of probed node types (expect ~120).
Done when: every one of the 12 languages has at least one probed class, function, import and call type, and the test names the language plus the node type on any failure.

tasks.title: index: extract part 2 — calls, inheritance, reference sites

details.goal: The second half of the extractor: every call site with its receiver, the inheritance edges, and the reference sites that make `references` edges possible — all table-driven.
details.contract:
Continues `src/indexer/extract.ts`; the shared types are fixed by TASK-041 and must not be changed. `sites.rs` fills the walk from `extract/mod.rs` and emits:
- `calls` edges for each `call_types` node: `target` is the callee's written name, `receiver` the text before the dot (or the object expression) when there is one, `local_name` empty, `line` the callee's line, `tier` `"extracted"` for a name written in source. A call with no resolvable callee name is NOT dropped: it becomes an `UnresolvedSite { evidence_kind: "dynamic", evidence: "call <written text>" }`, because the unresolved census is a payload contract.
- `inherits`/`implements` edges from `inheritance_types`: `inherits` for a class base, `implements` for an interface/trait list, the base name as written, `tier` `"extracted"`.
- `references` edges from the six `REFERENCE_SITES` shapes: `target` is the identifier, `evidence` names the site kind, `tier` `"extracted"` at this stage (binding decides later).
- `endpoint` nodes where the language convention marks a route handler (copy the TypeScript predicate verbatim; if it is language-specific, only emit for the languages that have it).
The walk is one traversal: do not re-parse, do not search ancestors per node more than once, and never allocate a string per visited node that no edge uses.
Tests: a snippet per family with a method call on a receiver (`a.b()`), a bare call (`f()`), a `new`/`object_creation`, a superclass, an interface implementation, a call argument reference, an assignment RHS reference, and a dynamic unresolvable call — asserting each edge kind, the receiver text, and the unresolved row.
steps: Port the call visitor with receiver extraction and the `new`/creation variants.
Port the inheritance visitors for both edge kinds.
Port the six reference-site shapes.
Port the endpoint predicate for the languages that have one.
Write the per-family tests including the unresolved row.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-index --test extract_sites` exits 0.
Done when: `a.b()` records `receiver: "a"` and `f()` records none, both inheritance kinds appear, and a dynamic call produces exactly one unresolved row with `evidence_kind: "dynamic"`.

tasks.title: index: binding — the four-step call resolution and the import taxonomy

details.goal: Turn raw edges into real edges with a tier, and record every failure BY CAUSE — the tier order and the evidence kinds are what `trace` reports and what the `eq` claim depends on.
details.contract:
Port `src/indexer/resolve.ts` (757 lines).
```rust
pub const EDGE_TIERS: [&str; 2] = ["extracted", "inferred"];
pub const BIND_EVIDENCE_KINDS: [&str; 4] = ["receiver_type_unknown", "ambiguous", "dynamic", "missing_module"];
pub struct SymbolIndex { /* nodes by qn, by name, by file; imports per file; bases per qn */ }
pub fn bind(units: &[FileUnit], index: &SymbolIndex) -> BindResult;   // {edges, unresolved}
```
Binding order per raw kind, exactly:
| raw kind | rule | tier |
|---|---|---|
| `contains` | target is already a qn | extracted |
| `inherits`/`implements` | `resolve_type_name` hit; miss -> unresolved `ambiguous` or `dynamic` | extracted |
| `references` | exactly one `nodes_named` hit; two or more are SILENTLY DROPPED; zero emits nothing | inferred |
| `calls` step 1 | exact qn in the same file (receiver as scope) | extracted |
| `calls` step 2 | name visible through the import table | extracted |
| `calls` step 3 | globally unique name | inferred |
| `calls` step 4 | superclass method for a typed receiver | inferred |
| ambiguity at steps 1/2/4 | unresolved `ambiguous` | — |
| fallthrough | `receiver_type_unknown` if a receiver was written, else `ambiguous` if several globals matched, else `dynamic` | — |
| `imports` | single `module_candidate` + target file node; >1 candidate -> `ambiguous` with the competing paths appended after the specifier; 0 candidates + a relative specifier -> `missing_module`; else `dynamic` | extracted |
Emit guard: never emit an edge whose `src` or `dst` is not in the index; dedupe on `file\u{0}kind\u{0}src\u{0}dst\u{0}line\u{0}local_name`.
Tests port `tests/resolve.test.ts`: every row of the table above, the silent drop for a multi-hit reference, the four evidence kinds with their `evidence` text, and the dedupe.
steps: Port the SymbolIndex builder (qn, names, per-file imports, bases).
Port the four-step call resolution with the ambiguity check at each step.
Port inherit/implements/references/contains/imports branches.
Port the emit guard and the dedupe key.
Write the table-driven tests.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-index --test resolve` exits 0 with at least one case per table row.
Done when: a two-candidate reference emits no edge, a relative import with no candidate yields `missing_module`, and a bare package specifier yields `dynamic`.

tasks.title: index: persist part 1 — one unit into the stage, tombstones

details.goal: Write one parsed file's rows into the stage inside the caller's transaction, and record what disappeared — the unit boundary is what makes an incremental run correct.
details.contract:
First half of `src/indexer/persist.ts` (830 lines); the second half is TASK-045 and both own `persist/`. Shared types:
```rust
pub struct PersistUnit { pub rel_path: String, pub nodes: Vec<ExtractedNode>, pub raw_edges: Vec<RawEdge>,
                         pub unresolved: Vec<UnresolvedSite>, pub not_indexed: Option<NotIndexedEntry> }
pub struct PersistCounts { pub file_id: i64, pub nodes: usize, pub edges: usize, pub unresolved: usize,
                           pub skipped_edges: usize, pub pending_tombstones: usize }
pub const PENDING_GENERATION: &str = "";
pub fn persist_unit(tx: &Transaction, unit: &PersistUnit, resolved: &BindResult) -> Result<PersistCounts>;
```
The SQL, verbatim (do not rewrite these as a builder):
```sql
DELETE FROM file WHERE path = ?
INSERT INTO file (path, language, sha256, size, line_count, parse_status, parse_error_ranges, indexed_generation)
  VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?) ON CONFLICT(path) DO UPDATE SET language = excluded.language, sha256 = excluded.sha256,
  size = excluded.size, line_count = excluded.line_count, parse_status = excluded.parse_status,
  parse_error_ranges = excluded.parse_error_ranges, indexed_generation = excluded.indexed_generation
DELETE FROM node|edge|unresolved WHERE file_id = (SELECT id FROM file WHERE path = ?)
DELETE FROM node WHERE qn = ? AND file_id <> ?
INSERT INTO node (file_id, kind, name, qn, start_line, end_line, signature, is_test, props) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?) RETURNING id
UPDATE node SET parent_id = ? WHERE id = ?
INSERT INTO edge (src_id, dst_id, kind, tier, file_id, line, local_name, evidence) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
INSERT INTO unresolved (file_id, line, raw_target, evidence_kind, evidence) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
DELETE FROM not_indexed WHERE path = ?
INSERT INTO not_indexed (path, reason, detail, language) VALUES (?,?,?,?) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
```
Plus the tombstone upsert (`INSERT ... SELECT n.qn, n.kind, n.file_id, ?, ?, (SELECT count(*) FROM edge e WHERE e.dst_id = n.id AND e.kind NOT IN ('contains','tested_by')) FROM node n JOIN file f ON f.id = n.file_id WHERE f.path = ? ON CONFLICT(qn) DO UPDATE SET ...`) run BEFORE the deletes, with `last_seen_generation = PENDING_GENERATION` and `removed_in_generation = ''`.
`RETURNING id` must return exactly one row — treat zero as an internal error naming the qn. Edges whose endpoints did not persist are counted in `skipped_edges`, never silently dropped.
Tests: insert then update the same file (ids stable where the qn is stable, deleted qns becoming tombstones), a unit with a `not_indexed` entry, an edge whose dst is missing (counted as skipped), and a conflict on the same qn in two files.
steps: Create `persist/mod.rs` with the shared types and the transaction seam (a `rusqlite::Transaction`, never a `Connection`).
Port the file upsert and the per-file deletes in the documented order.
Port node insert with `RETURNING id`, the parent update and the qn-conflict delete.
Port edge/unresolved/not_indexed inserts and the tombstone upsert.
Write the tests over a temp database.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-index --test persist_unit` exits 0.
Done when: re-persisting an unchanged file leaves the same node ids, and removing a symbol from a file produces exactly one tombstone row with `last_seen_generation = ''`.

tasks.title: index: the worker — lock, incremental routing, publish, exit codes

details.goal: The one process that owns the writer: take the lock or refuse, decide what actually changed, write every unit into a stage, publish atomically, and report through exactly four exit codes.
details.contract:
Port `src/indexer/worker.ts` (1054 lines).
```rust
pub enum WorkerMode { Full, Fast }
pub enum WorkerExit { Published = 0, Failed = 1, NothingToDo = 2, Locked = 75 }
pub fn run_worker(opts: &WorkerOptions) -> WorkerExit;   // never panics for a repository-level problem
```
Flow: acquire `<dataDir>/write.lock` (or return `Locked`), heartbeat at `STALE_AFTER_MS/4` = 15 s, `with_stage` (seeded from the live file when one exists), one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction covering tombstones -> file upserts -> drops -> `persist_unit` x N -> restore of the full resolved edge set -> coverage rewrite -> `finalize_generation` -> worker meta, then seal + publish, then release the lock, then write the run's telemetry record.
Incremental routing: `read_digests` (`SELECT path, sha256 FROM file ORDER BY path`), `read_previous_base_commit` (`SELECT base_commit FROM generation ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1`), `changed_since(...)`; `changed` = sha mismatch UNION git-reported, intersected with discovery; `removed` = file rows absent from discovery; `nothing_to_do = !force && changed == 0 && removed == 0`. A FAST run still rewrites the whole unit set (restore edges re-inserts the full resolved set) — copy that behaviour and its comment.
`file.parse_status` is `ok`/`failed`/`skipped` with `parse_error_ranges` as the joined strings; a failed parse still creates the file row so its symbols tombstone correctly. Git facts for identity: `rev-parse HEAD`, `symbolic-ref --short HEAD`, `config --get remote.origin.url` with the same prologue and the 10 s timeout; any failure is `None`, never an error.
Tests port `tests/worker.test.ts`: a first run publishes (exit 0), an immediate rerun returns `NothingToDo` (2), `--force` publishes again, a fast run after one file changed republishes only that unit but restores all edges, a concurrent lock holder yields 75, and a repository with zero parseable files still publishes with `files_indexed: 0`.
steps: Port the lock acquisition with the heartbeat and the four return paths.
Port discovery + digest comparison + git change detection into the routing decision.
Port the stage transaction: tombstones, upserts, units, restore, coverage, finalize.
Port identity capture and the run's telemetry record call (a no-op until phase_4).
Write the tests, including the concurrent-lock case with a second process holding the file.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-index --test worker` exits 0.
Done when: the four exit codes are each observed once, and a test asserts the live file's `sha256` is unchanged when the run returns `NothingToDo`.

tasks.title: Census parity: Rust indexes, TypeScript reads, numbers agree

details.goal: The write path's gate: a database built by the Rust indexer must be readable by the TypeScript binary, and its per-language census must match the TypeScript indexer's on the same corpus.
details.contract:
scripts/parity/census.ts runs under bun and prints, for any graph.db, the census as JSON: sqlite_version, files, nodes, edges_by_kind_tier, unresolved_by_kind, nodes_by_kind, nodes_by_language, not_indexed_by_reason, and the generation's seq, mode and status. It works on either implementation's database.
Counts are not enough. The parity bar makes array ORDER part of the contract (cursors index into a generation's stable ordering and rowids are minted by the writer), so the census also carries ORDERED ROW SEQUENCES for the six list-producing queries a page is taken from: node ids by rowid, edge ids by rowid, node_fts_state rowids, entryPoints(5) ids, hotspots(5) ids, and the findByName ids for a duplicated name. Compare them element by element; a count-only comparison would pass a writer that inserts in a different order and then invalidates every cursor.
Capture the TypeScript census for the polyglot and broken fixtures into rust/tests/golden/census/<fixture>.ts.json. cargo test -p sangkar-index --test census builds the same fixtures with the Rust worker and compares, printing a per-key delta table instead of a single mismatch.
Acceptance is a MEASURED delta: nodes, files, unresolved_by_kind and edges_by_kind_tier must match exactly per language, and every ordered sequence must match exactly. If a grammar substitution from TASK-038 makes a language differ, the test may allow that language a listed count delta, written into the golden as allowed_delta for that language with a comment naming the grammar version and repeated in the task report so it can reach .agents/prompts/gaps-n-future-works.md. An ordering difference is never allowed.
Record select sqlite_version() from both sides in the golden: FTS5 scoring and tie-breaks are version quantities, and the search ordering bm25 ASC, in_degree DESC, id ASC depends on them.
Also assert that the TypeScript binary's status answers from the Rust-built database with a non-null read_status.generation, which is the cross-implementation readability proof.
steps: Write census.ts as a database reader usable for both implementations, with the six ordered sequences and sqlite_version.
Capture the TypeScript censuses for both fixtures.
Build the fixtures with the Rust worker in the test and compare, printing the per-key delta table.
Encode any grammar-caused allowance explicitly and record both SQLite versions.
Run the TypeScript status against the Rust-built database and record the answer.
details.verify:
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-index --test census exits 0 with the delta table printed.
~/.bun/bin/bun run bin/sangkar.ts status --repo-root rust/tests/parity/fixtures/polyglot with --data-dir pointing at the Rust-built directory exits 0 and prints a generation.
Done when: polyglot shows zero unexplained delta, every allowed delta names its language and grammar version, and the six ordered sequences match.
